# round4.md — VisualCore Premium Procedural Games, Round 4
**Canonical root deliverable:** `round4.md` · **Proposed as of 2026-11-10** · **25 new premium games** · **complete only after `round3.md` implementation AND full D1/D2/D3 device campaign.**
**TRUTH STATUS:** This is a detailed engineering specification, not a report of implemented software. Original scores are subjective prior concept estimates; new supplemental scores are conservatively discounted analog estimates. No hardware performance, release, or app store success is claimed. All future pass claims must be supported by inspectable command/test outputs.
**Nonnegotiable invariants:** all hero artwork generated through code with VisualCore and GLES/ANGLE→Metal; no manual 3D assets, texture artists, image models, ads, tracking/ad SDKs, in-app purchases, subscriptions or mandatory network access; original paid-once offline play; do not use Claude CLI; Claude Desktop Code tab runs actual `/speckit-*` skills sequentially.

## Reading order and complete source-of-truth hierarchy
1. Read actual root CLAUDE.md and README.md and every preceding round file; verify installed .claude/skills and active feature location.
2. Independently verify the previous `round3.md` implementation lock and its 25×3 actual device outcomes. Absence or blocker means stop THIS round and resume earlier work.
3. Shared additions are proposed extensions, not directives to create duplicate packages. First inspect existing files and reuse established code; document any truly missing functions and consumers.
4. Use the exact 12 shared Spec Kit feature sequences before 25 game implementations, and the exact 10×8 game-feature prompts printed below.
5. Implement all targets and verify on host and simulators; only after a cryptographically hashed implementation-lock manifest run D1 whole round, then D2 whole round, then D3 whole round.
6. Keep the 25 complete argument outlines and 500-game baseline research notes in this file; evidence categories matter—no generic comparable is a sales forecast.

### 2.1 Shared public contracts and deterministic test hooks
```swift
public struct R4Seed: Codable, Hashable { public let value: UInt64 }
public struct R4Tick: Codable, Comparable { public var value: UInt64 }
public struct R4PuzzleAction: Codable {
    public let tick: UInt64; public let controlID: String
    public let normalizedCoordinates: SIMD2<Double>; public let value: Double
}
public struct R4RenderSnapshot: Codable {
    public let tick: UInt64; public let worldSeed: UInt64
    public let semanticObjectIDs: [UInt64]; public let qualityTier: Int
}
public protocol R4DeterministicGame {
    associatedtype State: Codable; associatedtype Action: Codable
    mutating func apply(_ action: Action) throws
    mutating func advanceFixedTick() throws
    func winPredicate() -> Bool
    func canonicalReplayDigest() -> String
}
// Adapt to audited actual existing VisualCore interfaces. NEVER duplicate
// render context or treat these illustrative interfaces as existing code.
```

```text
/speckit-constitution — Amend the existing VisualCore constitution specifically for Round 4, without deleting or weakening any existing requirements from README.md, CLAUDE.md, round2.md or rounds 3..3. Read actual source code and prior round convergence/device records before amending. Add enforceable principles: paid-once complete offline 3D games; no ads, advertising SDKs, tracking identifiers, IAP or subscriptions; no AI-generated images or hand modeled/painted hero assets; all visual effects written as procedural geometry, GLSL ES 3 shader programs, deterministic particles, fluids or analytic paths through the already-existing VisualCore → EGL/OpenGL ES → ANGLE's Metal backend. Preserve vendor forks and signing restrictions. Require independent CPU solver witnesses, 100 real content levels per proposed game, accessible interactions and distinct mechanics verified against the entire portfolio. Require all eight Spec Kit steps (specify/clarify/plan/checklist/tasks/analyze/implement/converge) for 12 incremental shared features and 250 game features; repeat implement + converge until real tests prove completion. Implementation + host/simulator verification must finish before a new implementation-lock manifest permits physical testing. Then test all 25 apps on D1, then D2, then D3, never update D3 from iPadOS 26.5. Device tests and market claims must cite actual evidence. No autonomous authority for Apple signing, login, billing, contract agreement, physical device permission, remote pushes outside owner standing approvals or release. Resolve routine ambiguities autonomously in written ADRs; do not invent success. Preserve this amendment with a dated constitution version and requirement traceability.

Existing math foundation: Numeric stability, deterministic integer ticks, explicit GLES caps and regression contracts. Solver/proof basis: Independent host/simulator verification of public packages and test evidence.
IMPLEMENTATION BOUNDARIES: use already built VisualCore public adapters and existing EGL/OpenGL ES/ANGLE Metal backend. Gameplay truth is CPU deterministic and separately serialized from render snapshots; shaders only portray truth. Premium complete offline app and clear distinct identity. Owner controls signing, device trust and App Store accounts.
SPEC KIT DISCIPLINE: invoke the installed actual skill inside Claude Desktop Code, inspect generated output in the expected spec directory and only advance based on a fresh real host/simulator evidence file. Record stable requirement IDs, owner decisions and dependency proofs; tag physical device work for AFTER complete implementation lock. Never claim hardware performance from simulator or plan text.
Enumerate all unresolved implementation choices in input model, camera/gesture timing, geometry representation, normals, shading, versioned persistence, level catalog, fallback paths and D3 resource caps. Resolve each autonomously using deterministic behavior and existing project patterns, starting with the recommended option; record decision and rejected alternatives. Never ask human routine questions. If source code contradicts the design, inspect and record its actual public API signatures; preserve previous completed features. Escalate only irreversible credentials/account actions. Record a date-stamped Clarifications entry with testable rationale and no hidden TODO.
```

## 4. Portfolio boundaries, previous-round gate and simulator/device split
- **MANDATORY PRECONDITION:** `round3.md` full implementation lock, 25 apps × three device outcomes, test provenance and final convergence complete. Verify hashes and logs; a nonexistent earlier round MUST block this one.
- **IMPLEMENTATION FIRST:** execute Round 4 shared features F01-F11; implement each of the 25 complete apps with all ten independent scoped Spec Kit feature flows; run macOS host, Linux-where-possible, iOS 26.5 and 27.2 simulator build and XCUITest. Physical device runs are forbidden until suite lock.
- **Physical device pass:** all 25 on D1 consecutively, then all 25 on D2, then all 25 on D3 without updating D3, through signed automation build, `xcrun devicectl`, JSON results, `xcodebuild` `.xcresult`, screen captures and thermal/frame evidence. Distinguish genuine pass, unsupported, failed, and owner blocked; skipped is never success.
- **Privacy:** no online gameplay, ad identifiers, app trackers, IAP, subscriptions, Apple account prompts, image-generation calls or licensed third-party art dependency. Shipping release must omit automation symbols; user-licensed fonts/system icons are okay if audited, not hero art.
- **Originality:** no near-identical products. Before release, prove each player goal/input/progression/visual metaphor is not merely a palette-swapped duplicate of another game in Round 1, 2 or this round.
- **Owner-only:** never alter signing teams/certificates, update D3, agree to commerce/legal terms or execute irreversible App Store publishing. A blocked item is marked honestly with next exact human step, not permission bypass.

## 5. Complete game-by-game implementation blueprints and per-feature Spec Kit commands
### 01. Icy Polyhedron — complete proposed implementation design (`R04-G01`)
**Source:** `G294`, source `Newly proposed 300; assessed from analog family prior`, conceptual score **93.84 /100**, proposed upfront price **$3.99**. *This is a design decision, not actual sales or in-engine measured quality.*
**One-sentence pitch:** Reconfigure edges of frozen solids while preserving volume. **Signature animated environment:** geometric frost geometry and glowing beveled edge networks; Beveled polyhedra, faceted signed-distance fields, instanced lattices and faux dispersion. **Core abstraction:** convex-solid graph.
#### 5.1.1. Product identity, audience, differentiation and non-goals
The player sees geometric frost geometry and glowing beveled edge networks; beveled polyhedra, faceted signed-distance fields, instanced lattices and faux dispersion, then learns that every luminous element represents an actual state variable of a puzzle built around the following verb: Reconfigure edges of frozen solids while preserving volume. The premium promise is one decisive, tactile 3D interaction, one clear target, satisfying action feedback and a complete offline catalog. No artificial wait timers, no ad gating, no login, no in-app purchases. The programmatic graphics are the product: the game must be more understandable **because** the particles, shadows, waves or solids move. Use SwiftUI only for menus and accessibility; real scene objects are driven by reusable VisualCore GLES/ANGLE draw paths.
This title must be uniquely distinguishable from other games by its `convex-solid graph` computational rules, visual `geometric frost geometry and glowing beveled edge networks; Beveled polyhedra, faceted signed-distance fields, instanced lattices and faux dispersion` and player control arrangement `Rotate/cut/exchange crystal solids to meet 3D geometry rules`. Create a side-by-side gameplay-differentiation table against all previously released VisualCore apps and the other 24 current concepts. Reject it if the input and goals could be reused unchanged by reskinning another application.
#### 5.1.2. Explicit mathematical state and success/failure rules
- **State model:** vertex planes n·x<=d; polytope clipping with epsilon-scaled robust predicates. Use fixed tick Δt=1/120s for normal logic (or 1/240 only if collision proof demands), with integer tick index and explicitly bounded control values. Serialize all source parameters as versioned codable data. No GPU or frame delta is authoritative for win/failure.
- **Player action:** Reconfigure edges of frozen solids while preserving volume. Normalize input into `IcyPolyhedronAction` tagged with stable control ID, tick, local scene coordinates and deterministic quantization. Illegal actions return typed `ActionRejected(reason, visualCue)` without changing state.
- **Win predicate:** place, cleave or rotate pieces until target mass/volume and adjacency topology match. For this particular product, all placed/checkpoint states must be satisfied concurrently and held for 6 fixed ticks, with no forbidden geometry contact or resource deficit. No shader-level visual similarity check substitutes for this predicate.
- **Failure predicate:** budget overrun, impossible state certificate, invalid component collisions, exhausted moves/time if explicitly signaled in the UI. Failure never silently corrupts a save or consumes premium content. Pause, undo and retry are always supported.
- **Solver:** exact discrete state BFS + convex clipping check on candidate action. It must output a machine-readable witness list of actions and resulting digest, prove a bounded path for every shipped level, and generate a contrasting invalid action for negative tests. Reject a level when no witness exists, multiple solutions violate an intentionally unique puzzle, or gesture targets are inaccessible.
- **Numeric risks:** zero-area faces, z-order transparencies, unmanifold mesh. Use safe clamp and finite checks, bounded loops, stable sorting of equal-key entities, seed-controlled randomness and approximate predication only where tolerance is exposed in metadata. A NaN, Inf, zero-timestep or unsolved rule must be a test failure.
#### 5.1.3. First session storyboard, user experience and precise input intent
- **00:00–00:15 — Orient:** Open on a precompiled real scene depicting geometric frost geometry and glowing beveled edge networks; Beveled polyhedra, faceted signed-distance fields, instanced lattices and faux dispersion; name the goal in under 12 words; color-independent icon for target; default silence is okay.
- **00:15–00:35 — One safe action:** Show a single draggable convex-solid graph handle; allow tap and hold, drag-release, and undo with immediate visual response. No camera action while dragging an object.
- **00:35–00:55 — Reveal the rule:** Expose a target with reconfigure edges of frozen solids while preserving volume; demonstrate the solver witness at quarter speed on repeatable seed without requiring a movie asset.
- **00:55–01:15 — First independent attempt:** Ask the player to complete one two-action challenge. A wrong action gets a preview and undo rather than confusing penalty.
- **01:15–01:35 — Reward and transition:** Present win state tied to authoritative convex-solid graph predicate; show actual new generated visual composition rather than a pre-rendered reward.
- **01:35–02:00 — Player control and trust:** Expose pause, reduce flashing/motion, camera reset and offline save state; restart resumes without an account.
**Touch:** Rotate/cut/exchange crystal solids to meet 3D geometry rules. Use one-finger object direct manipulation and a two-finger camera orbit, never allow unintentional camera movement while a target is captured. Minimum control size 44×44pt unless a physical-size, accessibility-audited alternative is provided. Offer focus cycling, keyboard controls where supported, descriptive VoiceOver state and noncolor target symbols. Camera pitch clamp, depth picking and undo are part of the contract.
#### 5.1.4. Renderer architecture, shader paths and actual code-generated visual recipe
**Geometry:** generated bevel prisms, layered facet reflection and gradient interiors. Create bounded indexed vertices from numeric state, shader variants determined at build time, stable draw order, backface choices, wireframe-like overlays where beneficial and a shared scene descriptor. The renderer consumes immutable snapshots and interpolates between previous and current tick; GPU floating-point differences never decide a puzzle result.
**Visual signature:** geometric frost geometry and glowing beveled edge networks; Beveled polyhedra, faceted signed-distance fields, instanced lattices and faux dispersion. To make this screenshot-worthy without asset artists: use curvature-based normals, a 3- or 4-stop analytical palette, thin edge emissive lighting, controlled depth-layer fog, instanced particle sparks, soft bloom in GLES3-safe framebuffer passes, and direct camera compositions. All texture-like detail comes from algebraic noise, ray-space gradients, distance-field contours or generated normals. Baked raster hero art is prohibited.
**GLES3 pipeline:** shared EGL surface & context from VisualCore; depth prepass or regular depth setup, opaque generated geometry, carefully sorted translucent geometry or weighted approximation only if available, emissive overlay, bounded separable blur, final color-management and UI composition. Rebuild resources after EGL context loss from CPU scene descriptor, not by reusing stale GL object handles. Establish 1×/2× adaptive sample budget after device evidence. Avoid unverified GLES extensions and always compile actual shader variants on both simulator toolchains.
**Numeric shader interface:** program ID `IcyPolyhedronScene`, `uTime` from fixed ticks, `uSeed` packed in stable integer uniforms, `uCamera`, `uQuality`, `uReduceMotion`, `uPaletteMode`, `IcyPolyhedronParams` uniform buffer equivalent compatible with audited ANGLE APIs. Validate all shader input domains and branch/loop bounds. Visual replay golden uses seed `d8041a475a2d` and camera manifest, generated on actual renderer.
#### 5.1.5. Content production, balancing, progression and rewards
- **World 01, levels 001–010:** introduce at most 1 distinct convex-solid graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `1`, cap solver depth at 14 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤145 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 02, levels 011–020:** introduce at most 1 distinct convex-solid graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `2`, cap solver depth at 18 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤160 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 03, levels 021–030:** introduce at most 1 distinct convex-solid graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `3`, cap solver depth at 22 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤175 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 04, levels 031–040:** introduce at most 2 distinct convex-solid graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `4`, cap solver depth at 26 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤190 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 05, levels 041–050:** introduce at most 2 distinct convex-solid graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `5`, cap solver depth at 30 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤205 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 06, levels 051–060:** introduce at most 2 distinct convex-solid graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `6`, cap solver depth at 34 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤220 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 07, levels 061–070:** introduce at most 3 distinct convex-solid graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `7`, cap solver depth at 38 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤235 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 08, levels 071–080:** introduce at most 3 distinct convex-solid graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `8`, cap solver depth at 42 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤250 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 09, levels 081–090:** introduce at most 3 distinct convex-solid graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `9`, cap solver depth at 46 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤265 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 10, levels 091–100:** introduce at most 4 distinct convex-solid graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `10`, cap solver depth at 50 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤280 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
Every generated level has explicit human-readable objective, difficulty, result predicate, move/action budget, certified solver replay, rejected-action certificate, loadable scene, display camera, accessibility annotations, visual-quality tiers, content checksum and stable persistent identifier. Generate the catalog offline during build, include compressed indexed payloads if needed, and ship no huge generated sources in Git. Prevent repeats by comparing canonical normalized puzzle hashes, not simply seed numbers. A title cannot ship with 100 colorful screens that lack gameplay or unique solutions.

Device observations cannot be prefilled in the document.

**Release policy:** premium one-time price, no ads, ad SDKs, IAP, subscriptions, external image assets or account dependence. If this game turns out too similar to another app, redesign or combine; do not publish reskins.

### 02. Crystal Phase Shift — complete proposed implementation design (`R04-G02`)
**Source:** `G301`, source `Newly proposed 300; assessed from analog family prior`, conceptual score **93.84 /100**, proposed upfront price **$3.99**. *This is a design decision, not actual sales or in-engine measured quality.*
**One-sentence pitch:** Change a mineral lattice phase to unlock a three-dimensional channel. **Signature animated environment:** tiny voxel cells snap into new reflective-looking structures; Beveled polyhedra, faceted signed-distance fields, instanced lattices and faux dispersion. **Core abstraction:** convex-solid graph.
#### 5.2.1. Product identity, audience, differentiation and non-goals
The player sees tiny voxel cells snap into new reflective-looking structures; beveled polyhedra, faceted signed-distance fields, instanced lattices and faux dispersion, then learns that every luminous element represents an actual state variable of a puzzle built around the following verb: Change a mineral lattice phase to unlock a three-dimensional channel. The premium promise is one decisive, tactile 3D interaction, one clear target, satisfying action feedback and a complete offline catalog. No artificial wait timers, no ad gating, no login, no in-app purchases. The programmatic graphics are the product: the game must be more understandable **because** the particles, shadows, waves or solids move. Use SwiftUI only for menus and accessibility; real scene objects are driven by reusable VisualCore GLES/ANGLE draw paths.
This title must be uniquely distinguishable from other games by its `convex-solid graph` computational rules, visual `tiny voxel cells snap into new reflective-looking structures; Beveled polyhedra, faceted signed-distance fields, instanced lattices and faux dispersion` and player control arrangement `Rotate/cut/exchange crystal solids to meet 3D geometry rules`. Create a side-by-side gameplay-differentiation table against all previously released VisualCore apps and the other 24 current concepts. Reject it if the input and goals could be reused unchanged by reskinning another application.
#### 5.2.2. Explicit mathematical state and success/failure rules
- **State model:** vertex planes n·x<=d; polytope clipping with epsilon-scaled robust predicates. Use fixed tick Δt=1/120s for normal logic (or 1/240 only if collision proof demands), with integer tick index and explicitly bounded control values. Serialize all source parameters as versioned codable data. No GPU or frame delta is authoritative for win/failure.
- **Player action:** Change a mineral lattice phase to unlock a three-dimensional channel. Normalize input into `CrystalPhaseShiftAction` tagged with stable control ID, tick, local scene coordinates and deterministic quantization. Illegal actions return typed `ActionRejected(reason, visualCue)` without changing state.
- **Win predicate:** place, cleave or rotate pieces until target mass/volume and adjacency topology match. For this particular product, all placed/checkpoint states must be satisfied concurrently and held for 8 fixed ticks, with no forbidden geometry contact or resource deficit. No shader-level visual similarity check substitutes for this predicate.
- **Failure predicate:** budget overrun, impossible state certificate, invalid component collisions, exhausted moves/time if explicitly signaled in the UI. Failure never silently corrupts a save or consumes premium content. Pause, undo and retry are always supported.
- **Solver:** exact discrete state BFS + convex clipping check on candidate action. It must output a machine-readable witness list of actions and resulting digest, prove a bounded path for every shipped level, and generate a contrasting invalid action for negative tests. Reject a level when no witness exists, multiple solutions violate an intentionally unique puzzle, or gesture targets are inaccessible.
- **Numeric risks:** zero-area faces, z-order transparencies, unmanifold mesh. Use safe clamp and finite checks, bounded loops, stable sorting of equal-key entities, seed-controlled randomness and approximate predication only where tolerance is exposed in metadata. A NaN, Inf, zero-timestep or unsolved rule must be a test failure.
#### 5.2.3. First session storyboard, user experience and precise input intent
- **00:00–00:15 — Orient:** Open on a precompiled real scene depicting tiny voxel cells snap into new reflective-looking structures; Beveled polyhedra, faceted signed-distance fields, instanced lattices and faux dispersion; name the goal in under 12 words; color-independent icon for target; default silence is okay.
- **00:15–00:35 — One safe action:** Show a single draggable convex-solid graph handle; allow tap and hold, drag-release, and undo with immediate visual response. No camera action while dragging an object.
- **00:35–00:55 — Reveal the rule:** Expose a target with change a mineral lattice phase to unlock a three-dimensional channel; demonstrate the solver witness at quarter speed on repeatable seed without requiring a movie asset.
- **00:55–01:15 — First independent attempt:** Ask the player to complete one two-action challenge. A wrong action gets a preview and undo rather than confusing penalty.
- **01:15–01:35 — Reward and transition:** Present win state tied to authoritative convex-solid graph predicate; show actual new generated visual composition rather than a pre-rendered reward.
- **01:35–02:00 — Player control and trust:** Expose pause, reduce flashing/motion, camera reset and offline save state; restart resumes without an account.
**Touch:** Rotate/cut/exchange crystal solids to meet 3D geometry rules. Use one-finger object direct manipulation and a two-finger camera orbit, never allow unintentional camera movement while a target is captured. Minimum control size 44×44pt unless a physical-size, accessibility-audited alternative is provided. Offer focus cycling, keyboard controls where supported, descriptive VoiceOver state and noncolor target symbols. Camera pitch clamp, depth picking and undo are part of the contract.
#### 5.2.4. Renderer architecture, shader paths and actual code-generated visual recipe
**Geometry:** generated bevel prisms, layered facet reflection and gradient interiors. Create bounded indexed vertices from numeric state, shader variants determined at build time, stable draw order, backface choices, wireframe-like overlays where beneficial and a shared scene descriptor. The renderer consumes immutable snapshots and interpolates between previous and current tick; GPU floating-point differences never decide a puzzle result.
**Visual signature:** tiny voxel cells snap into new reflective-looking structures; Beveled polyhedra, faceted signed-distance fields, instanced lattices and faux dispersion. To make this screenshot-worthy without asset artists: use curvature-based normals, a 3- or 4-stop analytical palette, thin edge emissive lighting, controlled depth-layer fog, instanced particle sparks, soft bloom in GLES3-safe framebuffer passes, and direct camera compositions. All texture-like detail comes from algebraic noise, ray-space gradients, distance-field contours or generated normals. Baked raster hero art is prohibited.
**GLES3 pipeline:** shared EGL surface & context from VisualCore; depth prepass or regular depth setup, opaque generated geometry, carefully sorted translucent geometry or weighted approximation only if available, emissive overlay, bounded separable blur, final color-management and UI composition. Rebuild resources after EGL context loss from CPU scene descriptor, not by reusing stale GL object handles. Establish 1×/2× adaptive sample budget after device evidence. Avoid unverified GLES extensions and always compile actual shader variants on both simulator toolchains.
**Numeric shader interface:** program ID `CrystalPhaseShiftScene`, `uTime` from fixed ticks, `uSeed` packed in stable integer uniforms, `uCamera`, `uQuality`, `uReduceMotion`, `uPaletteMode`, `CrystalPhaseShiftParams` uniform buffer equivalent compatible with audited ANGLE APIs. Validate all shader input domains and branch/loop bounds. Visual replay golden uses seed `d9471f65f7b3` and camera manifest, generated on actual renderer.
#### 5.2.5. Content production, balancing, progression and rewards
- **World 01, levels 001–010:** introduce at most 1 distinct convex-solid graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `1`, cap solver depth at 14 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤145 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 02, levels 011–020:** introduce at most 1 distinct convex-solid graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `2`, cap solver depth at 18 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤160 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.

- **World 05, levels 041–050:** introduce at most 2 distinct convex-solid graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `5`, cap solver depth at 30 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤205 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 06, levels 051–060:** introduce at most 2 distinct convex-solid graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `6`, cap solver depth at 34 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤220 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 07, levels 061–070:** introduce at most 3 distinct convex-solid graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `7`, cap solver depth at 38 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤235 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 08, levels 071–080:** introduce at most 3 distinct convex-solid graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `8`, cap solver depth at 42 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤250 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 09, levels 081–090:** introduce at most 3 distinct convex-solid graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `9`, cap solver depth at 46 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤265 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 10, levels 091–100:** introduce at most 4 distinct convex-solid graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `10`, cap solver depth at 50 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤280 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
Every generated level has explicit human-readable objective, difficulty, result predicate, move/action budget, certified solver replay, rejected-action certificate, loadable scene, display camera, accessibility annotations, visual-quality tiers, content checksum and stable persistent identifier. Generate the catalog offline during build, include compressed indexed payloads if needed, and ship no huge generated sources in Git. Prevent repeats by comparing canonical normalized puzzle hashes, not simply seed numbers. A title cannot ship with 100 colorful screens that lack gameplay or unique solutions.

### 03. Diamond Pulse — complete proposed implementation design (`R04-G03`)
**Source:** `G305`, source `Newly proposed 300; assessed from analog family prior`, conceptual score **93.81 /100**, proposed upfront price **$3.99**. *This is a design decision, not actual sales or in-engine measured quality.*
**One-sentence pitch:** Time crystal rotations so a traveling flash survives every split. **Signature animated environment:** fast staccato light cascades over geometric gemstone machinery; Beveled polyhedra, faceted signed-distance fields, instanced lattices and faux dispersion. **Core abstraction:** convex-solid graph.
#### 5.3.1. Product identity, audience, differentiation and non-goals
The player sees fast staccato light cascades over geometric gemstone machinery; beveled polyhedra, faceted signed-distance fields, instanced lattices and faux dispersion, then learns that every luminous element represents an actual state variable of a puzzle built around the following verb: Time crystal rotations so a traveling flash survives every split. The premium promise is one decisive, tactile 3D interaction, one clear target, satisfying action feedback and a complete offline catalog. No artificial wait timers, no ad gating, no login, no in-app purchases. The programmatic graphics are the product: the game must be more understandable **because** the particles, shadows, waves or solids move. Use SwiftUI only for menus and accessibility; real scene objects are driven by reusable VisualCore GLES/ANGLE draw paths.
This title must be uniquely distinguishable from other games by its `convex-solid graph` computational rules, visual `fast staccato light cascades over geometric gemstone machinery; Beveled polyhedra, faceted signed-distance fields, instanced lattices and faux dispersion` and player control arrangement `Rotate/cut/exchange crystal solids to meet 3D geometry rules`. Create a side-by-side gameplay-differentiation table against all previously released VisualCore apps and the other 24 current concepts. Reject it if the input and goals could be reused unchanged by reskinning another application.
#### 5.3.2. Explicit mathematical state and success/failure rules
- **State model:** vertex planes n·x<=d; polytope clipping with epsilon-scaled robust predicates. Use fixed tick Δt=1/120s for normal logic (or 1/240 only if collision proof demands), with integer tick index and explicitly bounded control values. Serialize all source parameters as versioned codable data. No GPU or frame delta is authoritative for win/failure.
- **Player action:** Time crystal rotations so a traveling flash survives every split. Normalize input into `DiamondPulseAction` tagged with stable control ID, tick, local scene coordinates and deterministic quantization. Illegal actions return typed `ActionRejected(reason, visualCue)` without changing state.
- **Win predicate:** place, cleave or rotate pieces until target mass/volume and adjacency topology match. For this particular product, all placed/checkpoint states must be satisfied concurrently and held for 7 fixed ticks, with no forbidden geometry contact or resource deficit. No shader-level visual similarity check substitutes for this predicate.
- **Failure predicate:** budget overrun, impossible state certificate, invalid component collisions, exhausted moves/time if explicitly signaled in the UI. Failure never silently corrupts a save or consumes premium content. Pause, undo and retry are always supported.
- **Solver:** exact discrete state BFS + convex clipping check on candidate action. It must output a machine-readable witness list of actions and resulting digest, prove a bounded path for every shipped level, and generate a contrasting invalid action for negative tests. Reject a level when no witness exists, multiple solutions violate an intentionally unique puzzle, or gesture targets are inaccessible.
- **Numeric risks:** zero-area faces, z-order transparencies, unmanifold mesh. Use safe clamp and finite checks, bounded loops, stable sorting of equal-key entities, seed-controlled randomness and approximate predication only where tolerance is exposed in metadata. A NaN, Inf, zero-timestep or unsolved rule must be a test failure.
#### 5.3.3. First session storyboard, user experience and precise input intent
- **00:00–00:15 — Orient:** Open on a precompiled real scene depicting fast staccato light cascades over geometric gemstone machinery; Beveled polyhedra, faceted signed-distance fields, instanced lattices and faux dispersion; name the goal in under 12 words; color-independent icon for target; default silence is okay.
- **00:15–00:35 — One safe action:** Show a single draggable convex-solid graph handle; allow tap and hold, drag-release, and undo with immediate visual response. No camera action while dragging an object.
- **00:35–00:55 — Reveal the rule:** Expose a target with time crystal rotations so a traveling flash survives every split; demonstrate the solver witness at quarter speed on repeatable seed without requiring a movie asset.
- **00:55–01:15 — First independent attempt:** Ask the player to complete one two-action challenge. A wrong action gets a preview and undo rather than confusing penalty.
- **01:15–01:35 — Reward and transition:** Present win state tied to authoritative convex-solid graph predicate; show actual new generated visual composition rather than a pre-rendered reward.
- **01:35–02:00 — Player control and trust:** Expose pause, reduce flashing/motion, camera reset and offline save state; restart resumes without an account.
**Touch:** Rotate/cut/exchange crystal solids to meet 3D geometry rules. Use one-finger object direct manipulation and a two-finger camera orbit, never allow unintentional camera movement while a target is captured. Minimum control size 44×44pt unless a physical-size, accessibility-audited alternative is provided. Offer focus cycling, keyboard controls where supported, descriptive VoiceOver state and noncolor target symbols. Camera pitch clamp, depth picking and undo are part of the contract.
#### 5.3.4. Renderer architecture, shader paths and actual code-generated visual recipe
**Geometry:** generated bevel prisms, layered facet reflection and gradient interiors. Create bounded indexed vertices from numeric state, shader variants determined at build time, stable draw order, backface choices, wireframe-like overlays where beneficial and a shared scene descriptor. The renderer consumes immutable snapshots and interpolates between previous and current tick; GPU floating-point differences never decide a puzzle result.
**Visual signature:** fast staccato light cascades over geometric gemstone machinery; Beveled polyhedra, faceted signed-distance fields, instanced lattices and faux dispersion. To make this screenshot-worthy without asset artists: use curvature-based normals, a 3- or 4-stop analytical palette, thin edge emissive lighting, controlled depth-layer fog, instanced particle sparks, soft bloom in GLES3-safe framebuffer passes, and direct camera compositions. All texture-like detail comes from algebraic noise, ray-space gradients, distance-field contours or generated normals. Baked raster hero art is prohibited.
**GLES3 pipeline:** shared EGL surface & context from VisualCore; depth prepass or regular depth setup, opaque generated geometry, carefully sorted translucent geometry or weighted approximation only if available, emissive overlay, bounded separable blur, final color-management and UI composition. Rebuild resources after EGL context loss from CPU scene descriptor, not by reusing stale GL object handles. Establish 1×/2× adaptive sample budget after device evidence. Avoid unverified GLES extensions and always compile actual shader variants on both simulator toolchains.
**Numeric shader interface:** program ID `DiamondPulseScene`, `uTime` from fixed ticks, `uSeed` packed in stable integer uniforms, `uCamera`, `uQuality`, `uReduceMotion`, `uPaletteMode`, `DiamondPulseParams` uniform buffer equivalent compatible with audited ANGLE APIs. Validate all shader input domains and branch/loop bounds. Visual replay golden uses seed `7d7fde9d2c72` and camera manifest, generated on actual renderer.
#### 5.3.5. Content production, balancing, progression and rewards
- **World 01, levels 001–010:** introduce at most 1 distinct convex-solid graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `1`, cap solver depth at 14 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤145 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 02, levels 011–020:** introduce at most 1 distinct convex-solid graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `2`, cap solver depth at 18 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤160 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.

- **World 05, levels 041–050:** introduce at most 2 distinct convex-solid graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `5`, cap solver depth at 30 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤205 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 06, levels 051–060:** introduce at most 2 distinct convex-solid graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `6`, cap solver depth at 34 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤220 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 07, levels 061–070:** introduce at most 3 distinct convex-solid graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `7`, cap solver depth at 38 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤235 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 08, levels 071–080:** introduce at most 3 distinct convex-solid graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `8`, cap solver depth at 42 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤250 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 09, levels 081–090:** introduce at most 3 distinct convex-solid graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `9`, cap solver depth at 46 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤265 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 10, levels 091–100:** introduce at most 4 distinct convex-solid graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `10`, cap solver depth at 50 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤280 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
Every generated level has explicit human-readable objective, difficulty, result predicate, move/action budget, certified solver replay, rejected-action certificate, loadable scene, display camera, accessibility annotations, visual-quality tiers, content checksum and stable persistent identifier. Generate the catalog offline during build, include compressed indexed payloads if needed, and ship no huge generated sources in Git. Prevent repeats by comparing canonical normalized puzzle hashes, not simply seed numbers. A title cannot ship with 100 colorful screens that lack gameplay or unique solutions.

**Scope:** Implement exact game state, action sanitization, illegal move failures and win predicates; no renderer-owned truth. **Inputs and decisions:** Time crystal rotations so a traveling flash survives every split. **Physics contract:** vertex planes n·x<=d; polytope clipping with epsilon-scaled robust predicates. **Renderer identity:** fast staccato light cascades over geometric gemstone machinery; Beveled polyhedra, faceted signed-distance fields, instanced lattices and faux dispersion. **Pass gate:** solver witnesses, test commands and intended source files are inspectable.

### 04. Octahedral Orchard — complete proposed implementation design (`R04-G04`)
**Source:** `G296`, source `Newly proposed 300; assessed from analog family prior`, conceptual score **93.79 /100**, proposed upfront price **$3.99**. *This is a design decision, not actual sales or in-engine measured quality.*
**One-sentence pitch:** Connect branching octahedron clusters into a stable luminous canopy. **Signature animated environment:** glowing Platonic solid growth and spectral shadow play; Beveled polyhedra, faceted signed-distance fields, instanced lattices and faux dispersion. **Core abstraction:** convex-solid graph.
#### 5.4.1. Product identity, audience, differentiation and non-goals
The player sees glowing platonic solid growth and spectral shadow play; beveled polyhedra, faceted signed-distance fields, instanced lattices and faux dispersion, then learns that every luminous element represents an actual state variable of a puzzle built around the following verb: Connect branching octahedron clusters into a stable luminous canopy. The premium promise is one decisive, tactile 3D interaction, one clear target, satisfying action feedback and a complete offline catalog. No artificial wait timers, no ad gating, no login, no in-app purchases. The programmatic graphics are the product: the game must be more understandable **because** the particles, shadows, waves or solids move. Use SwiftUI only for menus and accessibility; real scene objects are driven by reusable VisualCore GLES/ANGLE draw paths.
This title must be uniquely distinguishable from other games by its `convex-solid graph` computational rules, visual `glowing Platonic solid growth and spectral shadow play; Beveled polyhedra, faceted signed-distance fields, instanced lattices and faux dispersion` and player control arrangement `Rotate/cut/exchange crystal solids to meet 3D geometry rules`. Create a side-by-side gameplay-differentiation table against all previously released VisualCore apps and the other 24 current concepts. Reject it if the input and goals could be reused unchanged by reskinning another application.
#### 5.4.2. Explicit mathematical state and success/failure rules
- **State model:** vertex planes n·x<=d; polytope clipping with epsilon-scaled robust predicates. Use fixed tick Δt=1/120s for normal logic (or 1/240 only if collision proof demands), with integer tick index and explicitly bounded control values. Serialize all source parameters as versioned codable data. No GPU or frame delta is authoritative for win/failure.
- **Player action:** Connect branching octahedron clusters into a stable luminous canopy. Normalize input into `OctahedralOrchardAction` tagged with stable control ID, tick, local scene coordinates and deterministic quantization. Illegal actions return typed `ActionRejected(reason, visualCue)` without changing state.
- **Win predicate:** place, cleave or rotate pieces until target mass/volume and adjacency topology match. For this particular product, all placed/checkpoint states must be satisfied concurrently and held for 8 fixed ticks, with no forbidden geometry contact or resource deficit. No shader-level visual similarity check substitutes for this predicate.
- **Failure predicate:** budget overrun, impossible state certificate, invalid component collisions, exhausted moves/time if explicitly signaled in the UI. Failure never silently corrupts a save or consumes premium content. Pause, undo and retry are always supported.
- **Solver:** exact discrete state BFS + convex clipping check on candidate action. It must output a machine-readable witness list of actions and resulting digest, prove a bounded path for every shipped level, and generate a contrasting invalid action for negative tests. Reject a level when no witness exists, multiple solutions violate an intentionally unique puzzle, or gesture targets are inaccessible.
- **Numeric risks:** zero-area faces, z-order transparencies, unmanifold mesh. Use safe clamp and finite checks, bounded loops, stable sorting of equal-key entities, seed-controlled randomness and approximate predication only where tolerance is exposed in metadata. A NaN, Inf, zero-timestep or unsolved rule must be a test failure.
#### 5.4.3. First session storyboard, user experience and precise input intent
- **00:00–00:15 — Orient:** Open on a precompiled real scene depicting glowing Platonic solid growth and spectral shadow play; Beveled polyhedra, faceted signed-distance fields, instanced lattices and faux dispersion; name the goal in under 12 words; color-independent icon for target; default silence is okay.
- **00:15–00:35 — One safe action:** Show a single draggable convex-solid graph handle; allow tap and hold, drag-release, and undo with immediate visual response. No camera action while dragging an object.
- **00:35–00:55 — Reveal the rule:** Expose a target with connect branching octahedron clusters into a stable luminous canopy; demonstrate the solver witness at quarter speed on repeatable seed without requiring a movie asset.
- **00:55–01:15 — First independent attempt:** Ask the player to complete one two-action challenge. A wrong action gets a preview and undo rather than confusing penalty.
- **01:15–01:35 — Reward and transition:** Present win state tied to authoritative convex-solid graph predicate; show actual new generated visual composition rather than a pre-rendered reward.
- **01:35–02:00 — Player control and trust:** Expose pause, reduce flashing/motion, camera reset and offline save state; restart resumes without an account.
**Touch:** Rotate/cut/exchange crystal solids to meet 3D geometry rules. Use one-finger object direct manipulation and a two-finger camera orbit, never allow unintentional camera movement while a target is captured. Minimum control size 44×44pt unless a physical-size, accessibility-audited alternative is provided. Offer focus cycling, keyboard controls where supported, descriptive VoiceOver state and noncolor target symbols. Camera pitch clamp, depth picking and undo are part of the contract.
#### 5.4.4. Renderer architecture, shader paths and actual code-generated visual recipe
**Geometry:** generated bevel prisms, layered facet reflection and gradient interiors. Create bounded indexed vertices from numeric state, shader variants determined at build time, stable draw order, backface choices, wireframe-like overlays where beneficial and a shared scene descriptor. The renderer consumes immutable snapshots and interpolates between previous and current tick; GPU floating-point differences never decide a puzzle result.
**Visual signature:** glowing Platonic solid growth and spectral shadow play; Beveled polyhedra, faceted signed-distance fields, instanced lattices and faux dispersion. To make this screenshot-worthy without asset artists: use curvature-based normals, a 3- or 4-stop analytical palette, thin edge emissive lighting, controlled depth-layer fog, instanced particle sparks, soft bloom in GLES3-safe framebuffer passes, and direct camera compositions. All texture-like detail comes from algebraic noise, ray-space gradients, distance-field contours or generated normals. Baked raster hero art is prohibited.
**GLES3 pipeline:** shared EGL surface & context from VisualCore; depth prepass or regular depth setup, opaque generated geometry, carefully sorted translucent geometry or weighted approximation only if available, emissive overlay, bounded separable blur, final color-management and UI composition. Rebuild resources after EGL context loss from CPU scene descriptor, not by reusing stale GL object handles. Establish 1×/2× adaptive sample budget after device evidence. Avoid unverified GLES extensions and always compile actual shader variants on both simulator toolchains.
**Numeric shader interface:** program ID `OctahedralOrchardScene`, `uTime` from fixed ticks, `uSeed` packed in stable integer uniforms, `uCamera`, `uQuality`, `uReduceMotion`, `uPaletteMode`, `OctahedralOrchardParams` uniform buffer equivalent compatible with audited ANGLE APIs. Validate all shader input domains and branch/loop bounds. Visual replay golden uses seed `be8b0dc787cf` and camera manifest, generated on actual renderer.
#### 5.4.5. Content production, balancing, progression and rewards
- **World 01, levels 001–010:** introduce at most 1 distinct convex-solid graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `1`, cap solver depth at 14 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤145 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 02, levels 011–020:** introduce at most 1 distinct convex-solid graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `2`, cap solver depth at 18 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤160 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.

- **World 05, levels 041–050:** introduce at most 2 distinct convex-solid graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `5`, cap solver depth at 30 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤205 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 06, levels 051–060:** introduce at most 2 distinct convex-solid graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `6`, cap solver depth at 34 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤220 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 07, levels 061–070:** introduce at most 3 distinct convex-solid graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `7`, cap solver depth at 38 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤235 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 08, levels 071–080:** introduce at most 3 distinct convex-solid graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `8`, cap solver depth at 42 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤250 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 09, levels 081–090:** introduce at most 3 distinct convex-solid graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `9`, cap solver depth at 46 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤265 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 10, levels 091–100:** introduce at most 4 distinct convex-solid graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `10`, cap solver depth at 50 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤280 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
Every generated level has explicit human-readable objective, difficulty, result predicate, move/action budget, certified solver replay, rejected-action certificate, loadable scene, display camera, accessibility annotations, visual-quality tiers, content checksum and stable persistent identifier. Generate the catalog offline during build, include compressed indexed payloads if needed, and ship no huge generated sources in Git. Prevent repeats by comparing canonical normalized puzzle hashes, not simply seed numbers. A title cannot ship with 100 colorful screens that lack gameplay or unique solutions.

### 05. Echo Harmonics — complete proposed implementation design (`R04-G05`)
**Source:** `G469`, source `Newly proposed 300; assessed from analog family prior`, conceptual score **93.78 /100**, proposed upfront price **$2.99**. *This is a design decision, not actual sales or in-engine measured quality.*
**One-sentence pitch:** Adjust frequency bands to expose a hidden geometric object. **Signature animated environment:** translucent waves reveal resonant contours on solids; Analytic oscillators, Fourier curve meshes, interference heightfields and emissive color. **Core abstraction:** harmonic field.
#### 5.5.1. Product identity, audience, differentiation and non-goals
The player sees translucent waves reveal resonant contours on solids; analytic oscillators, fourier curve meshes, interference heightfields and emissive color, then learns that every luminous element represents an actual state variable of a puzzle built around the following verb: Adjust frequency bands to expose a hidden geometric object. The premium promise is one decisive, tactile 3D interaction, one clear target, satisfying action feedback and a complete offline catalog. No artificial wait timers, no ad gating, no login, no in-app purchases. The programmatic graphics are the product: the game must be more understandable **because** the particles, shadows, waves or solids move. Use SwiftUI only for menus and accessibility; real scene objects are driven by reusable VisualCore GLES/ANGLE draw paths.
This title must be uniquely distinguishable from other games by its `harmonic field` computational rules, visual `translucent waves reveal resonant contours on solids; Analytic oscillators, Fourier curve meshes, interference heightfields and emissive color` and player control arrangement `Tune harmonics and phase to achieve a target three-dimensional pattern`. Create a side-by-side gameplay-differentiation table against all previously released VisualCore apps and the other 24 current concepts. Reject it if the input and goals could be reused unchanged by reskinning another application.
#### 5.5.2. Explicit mathematical state and success/failure rules
- **State model:** u(t)=Σ A_i sin(ω_i t+φ_i) and 3D path sampling; quantize ω_i ratios and phases. Use fixed tick Δt=1/120s for normal logic (or 1/240 only if collision proof demands), with integer tick index and explicitly bounded control values. Serialize all source parameters as versioned codable data. No GPU or frame delta is authoritative for win/failure.
- **Player action:** Adjust frequency bands to expose a hidden geometric object. Normalize input into `EchoHarmonicsAction` tagged with stable control ID, tick, local scene coordinates and deterministic quantization. Illegal actions return typed `ActionRejected(reason, visualCue)` without changing state.
- **Win predicate:** a sampled curve must visit target waypoints in order while avoiding forbidden volumes. For this particular product, all placed/checkpoint states must be satisfied concurrently and held for 7 fixed ticks, with no forbidden geometry contact or resource deficit. No shader-level visual similarity check substitutes for this predicate.
- **Failure predicate:** budget overrun, impossible state certificate, invalid component collisions, exhausted moves/time if explicitly signaled in the UI. Failure never silently corrupts a save or consumes premium content. Pause, undo and retry are always supported.
- **Solver:** bounded integer-frequency enumeration + adaptive swept-segment collision. It must output a machine-readable witness list of actions and resulting digest, prove a bounded path for every shipped level, and generate a contrasting invalid action for negative tests. Reject a level when no witness exists, multiple solutions violate an intentionally unique puzzle, or gesture targets are inaccessible.
- **Numeric risks:** phase wrapping, singular derivative, aliased camera under grazing views. Use safe clamp and finite checks, bounded loops, stable sorting of equal-key entities, seed-controlled randomness and approximate predication only where tolerance is exposed in metadata. A NaN, Inf, zero-timestep or unsolved rule must be a test failure.
#### 5.5.3. First session storyboard, user experience and precise input intent
- **00:00–00:15 — Orient:** Open on a precompiled real scene depicting translucent waves reveal resonant contours on solids; Analytic oscillators, Fourier curve meshes, interference heightfields and emissive color; name the goal in under 12 words; color-independent icon for target; default silence is okay.
- **00:15–00:35 — One safe action:** Show a single draggable harmonic field handle; allow tap and hold, drag-release, and undo with immediate visual response. No camera action while dragging an object.
- **00:35–00:55 — Reveal the rule:** Expose a target with adjust frequency bands to expose a hidden geometric object; demonstrate the solver witness at quarter speed on repeatable seed without requiring a movie asset.
- **00:55–01:15 — First independent attempt:** Ask the player to complete one two-action challenge. A wrong action gets a preview and undo rather than confusing penalty.
- **01:15–01:35 — Reward and transition:** Present win state tied to authoritative harmonic field predicate; show actual new generated visual composition rather than a pre-rendered reward.
- **01:35–02:00 — Player control and trust:** Expose pause, reduce flashing/motion, camera reset and offline save state; restart resumes without an account.
**Touch:** Tune harmonics and phase to achieve a target three-dimensional pattern. Use one-finger object direct manipulation and a two-finger camera orbit, never allow unintentional camera movement while a target is captured. Minimum control size 44×44pt unless a physical-size, accessibility-audited alternative is provided. Offer focus cycling, keyboard controls where supported, descriptive VoiceOver state and noncolor target symbols. Camera pitch clamp, depth picking and undo are part of the contract.
#### 5.5.4. Renderer architecture, shader paths and actual code-generated visual recipe
**Geometry:** parallel-transport ribbons, interference color and normal-based emission. Create bounded indexed vertices from numeric state, shader variants determined at build time, stable draw order, backface choices, wireframe-like overlays where beneficial and a shared scene descriptor. The renderer consumes immutable snapshots and interpolates between previous and current tick; GPU floating-point differences never decide a puzzle result.
**Visual signature:** translucent waves reveal resonant contours on solids; Analytic oscillators, Fourier curve meshes, interference heightfields and emissive color. To make this screenshot-worthy without asset artists: use curvature-based normals, a 3- or 4-stop analytical palette, thin edge emissive lighting, controlled depth-layer fog, instanced particle sparks, soft bloom in GLES3-safe framebuffer passes, and direct camera compositions. All texture-like detail comes from algebraic noise, ray-space gradients, distance-field contours or generated normals. Baked raster hero art is prohibited.
**GLES3 pipeline:** shared EGL surface & context from VisualCore; depth prepass or regular depth setup, opaque generated geometry, carefully sorted translucent geometry or weighted approximation only if available, emissive overlay, bounded separable blur, final color-management and UI composition. Rebuild resources after EGL context loss from CPU scene descriptor, not by reusing stale GL object handles. Establish 1×/2× adaptive sample budget after device evidence. Avoid unverified GLES extensions and always compile actual shader variants on both simulator toolchains.
**Numeric shader interface:** program ID `EchoHarmonicsScene`, `uTime` from fixed ticks, `uSeed` packed in stable integer uniforms, `uCamera`, `uQuality`, `uReduceMotion`, `uPaletteMode`, `EchoHarmonicsParams` uniform buffer equivalent compatible with audited ANGLE APIs. Validate all shader input domains and branch/loop bounds. Visual replay golden uses seed `a696a0b7dd9e` and camera manifest, generated on actual renderer.
#### 5.5.5. Content production, balancing, progression and rewards
- **World 01, levels 001–010:** introduce at most 1 distinct harmonic field controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `1`, cap solver depth at 14 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤145 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 02, levels 011–020:** introduce at most 1 distinct harmonic field controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `2`, cap solver depth at 18 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤160 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 03, levels 021–030:** introduce at most 1 distinct harmonic field controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `3`, cap solver depth at 22 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤175 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 04, levels 031–040:** introduce at most 2 distinct harmonic field controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `4`, cap solver depth at 26 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤190 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 05, levels 041–050:** introduce at most 2 distinct harmonic field controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `5`, cap solver depth at 30 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤205 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 06, levels 051–060:** introduce at most 2 distinct harmonic field controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `6`, cap solver depth at 34 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤220 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 07, levels 061–070:** introduce at most 3 distinct harmonic field controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `7`, cap solver depth at 38 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤235 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 08, levels 071–080:** introduce at most 3 distinct harmonic field controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `8`, cap solver depth at 42 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤250 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 09, levels 081–090:** introduce at most 3 distinct harmonic field controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `9`, cap solver depth at 46 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤265 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 10, levels 091–100:** introduce at most 4 distinct harmonic field controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `10`, cap solver depth at 50 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤280 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
Every generated level has explicit human-readable objective, difficulty, result predicate, move/action budget, certified solver replay, rejected-action certificate, loadable scene, display camera, accessibility annotations, visual-quality tiers, content checksum and stable persistent identifier. Generate the catalog offline during build, include compressed indexed payloads if needed, and ship no huge generated sources in Git. Prevent repeats by comparing canonical normalized puzzle hashes, not simply seed numbers. A title cannot ship with 100 colorful screens that lack gameplay or unique solutions.
